# Keep a single tracked timer for a no-window offscreen notification wait

For a no-currentWindow offscreen wait, each qualifying callback assigns a fresh setInterval(callback,5000) without checking an existing interval; only the latest stored handle is cleared. Repeated offscreen callbacks can therefore leave an older handle beyond this cleanup. A focused fake-timer test should keep one polling handle while offscreen and remove all handles on settlement/reset. No timer-count experiment ran. The related current id field begins null and is assigned only inside the already-truthy/different-id branch; broader notification replacement behavior remains a separate unexecuted scope, not a proven cause. Full earlier D239335 discussion remains unavailable. This is a public source-only scoped investigation/test proposal, not an accepted new rule or executed failure.

Scope: In-app notification scheduler cancellation and resource lifetime.
